newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firm on physicals.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil firm on physicals.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were stable on Tuesday and were expected to rise later as physical undertone remained firm, traders and brokers said.
They said a strong crude market also helped to prop up prices.
IPE June Brent crude rose 40 cents to close in London at $18.34 and was quited within range on SIMEX.
Brokers said May gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.80/26.00 little changed from Monday. June was indicated at $24.40/$24.60, up 5-10 cents from Monday.

"The cash market is firm with some healthy buying interest seen yesterday," one trader said. "That removes some of the earlier uncertainties of whether the buying support in the last few weeks would continue."
"Tender demand from Sri Lanka and anticipations of India's demand would also help prop sentiment," a broker said.
But talks on the fuel oil swaps were thin as some players were away attending an industry function marking the relaunch of the SIMEX fuel oil contract.
Fuel oil traders and brokers said they would be watching trades on SIMEX later Tuesday when the revised fuel oil contract is launched at 1430 GMT.
Fuel oil swaps quotes were unchanged from Monday with May quoted at $97.50/98.50.
